title: A Crocodile Swam 590 Kilometres Across the Open Ocean

scenes.text: A crocodile swam 590 kilometres across the open ocean.
Scientists tracked it by satellite: twenty-five days at sea, off the coast of Australia.
It didn't paddle the whole way. It set off when the tide turned and let the current carry it.
When the tide turned against it, it rested on the riverbank. Another waited four days for the water to flip.
So a crocodile crossed an ocean, and the ocean did most of the work.

description:
A saltwater crocodile tracked by satellite swam 590 kilometres across open sea in 25 days.
Researchers found the giant reptiles time their trips to ride tides and surface currents, then rest on riverbanks when the flow turns against them. A second crocodile covered more than 411 kilometres in 20 days.
Would you swim in water where one of these might be cruising past?

first_comment: The big one in the study was 4.8 metres long and waited four days in a sheltered bay until the current turned. Patience beats paddling. Would you have waited?
